action: Wrote down the properties that every step of the reported construction uses: kernels of its Equation (3.6), a leading-order limit given coordinate by coordinate by the pairwise sign model of its Equation (3.2), and parity factors of pairs of points lying in two faces as the only nonconstant limiting terms. Defined the sign model M_H of a general bipartite pattern for arbitrary face sizes, named the conditional assumption RL(H), and proved that the optimum of the admissible family equals the Sidorenko value on every girth-six pattern: M_H is identically 1 without 4-cycles (Lemma O), so the construction density and its symmetrization tend to (E V_q)^{e(H)} for every finite data (Corollary O prime, with the coordinate factorization and the normalization written out). Checked tightness: on every pattern with a 4-cycle M_H takes the values 0 and 2. The proof file sign-model-obstruction.md in the proofs directory was drafted during the exploration and checked against the full text of the reported counterexample and completed in this move.
output: A barrier theorem: no finite data of the reported construction produces a leading-order deficit on any bipartite pattern of girth at least six, conditional on RL(H); in particular none on the girth-six patterns outside C_2. The property the girth-six patterns lack is a pair of points in two faces, that is, a 4-cycle. The direction of the node is unreachable for this class; the premise outside C_2 itself is neither proved nor refuted.
